verdict.rationale: OpenClaw's built-in Automations support event triggers beyond schedules: inbound Gateway HTTP hooks, Gmail PubSub and IMAP email triggers. Standing orders also give the agent permanent operating authority for defined programs, so event-driven actions are a first-party capability. However, the evidence never documents a declarative rule layer (conditions or filters mapping specific events to specific actions), and event sources appear limited to webhooks and email. missing for 10: documented rule/condition definition syntax for event-to-action mapping, breadth of event sources beyond webhooks/Gmail/IMAP, independent or hands-on corroboration of event-triggered automations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Automations: scheduled jobs, webhooks, and Gmail PubSub triggers for the Gateway scheduler
Gateway HTTP hooks let an external service wake an agent or submit an agent turn.
Standing orders grant your agent **permanent operating authority** for defined programs.
